title: RSA exponentiation identity modulo a prime
statement: Let $p$ be a prime, and let $q, m, e, d, k$ be natural numbers satisfying $ed = 1 + k(p-1)(q-1)$. Then $m^{ed} \equiv m \pmod{p}$; that is, the images of $m^{ed}$ and $m$ agree in $\bbz/p\bbz$.
hypotheses_covered: $q, m, e, d, k$ are natural numbers
replaced:
If $p$ is prime and $ed = 1 + k(p-1)(q-1)$, then $m^{ed} \equiv m$ in $\bbz/p\bbz$ for every
$m \in \bbn$.
